analysis.investment_thesis: Capillary is an enterprise loyalty SaaS with impressive 36.7% revenue CAGR that just turned EBITDA-positive in FY25 — but at ₹4,492 Cr market cap and 420x P/E on a mere ₹13 Cr net profit, the price is violently wrong for my SMILE framework. This is a story I'd love at 10x lower market cap; at current levels, you're paying for perfection on a company still burning free cash flow.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 36.7% (FY21-25) with EBITDA inflection from -56 Cr in FY23 to +72 Cr in FY25 — genuine operational turnaround
Low D/E of 0.17 with cash of ₹201 Cr — balance sheet is clean post the long loss-making phase
Promoter holding at 52.23% crosses my 50% threshold — skin in the game intact
key_risks: Market cap of ₹4,492 Cr is 4-5x my sweet spot — information asymmetry advantage is gone, DII already own 18.6%
P/E of 420x on ₹13 Cr net profit is speculation masquerading as investing — any earnings miss collapses the valuation
Free cash flow was -₹94 Cr in FY25 despite ₹72 Cr EBITDA — working capital or capitalised costs are silently consuming cash
red_flags: Market cap ₹4,492 Cr — 4-5x outside my ₹100-1,000 Cr sweet spot
P/E 420x vs my threshold of 8-15x for small-caps
Gross margin 35.5% is dangerously low for a company positioning itself as SaaS (peers run 65-80%)
FCF was -₹94 Cr in FY25 despite positive EBITDA — cash conversion is broken
Company lost ₹-269 Cr cumulatively from FY21-FY24; single year of ₹13 Cr profit is too thin to justify this valuation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Capillary fails the SMILE test on the two most critical parameters: Size and Entry Price. At ₹4,492 Cr, it is a mid-cap — institutions have already discovered it (DII 18.6%), so the information asymmetry that creates multibaggers is absent. The valuation at 420x P/E and 6.97x P/B for a company earning just ₹13 Cr net profit is priced for a decade of flawless execution. A single quarter of revenue slowdown or margin pressure could cause a 40-50% drawdown from these levels.

The underlying business does show genuine promise — the EBITDA turnaround from -₹56 Cr to +₹72 Cr in two years signals real operating leverage, and the loyalty/CRM SaaS TAM globally is enormous. However, the 35.5% gross margin is a structural concern (true SaaS businesses run 65-80%), and the FCF of -₹94 Cr in FY25 despite ₹72 Cr EBITDA suggests high capitalised software costs or working capital drag that the P&L flatters. I would track this from the sidelines and revisit only if market cap falls below ₹800 Cr or the FCF conversion turns demonstrably positive for 2-3 consecutive years.
